argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the canonical balanced filtration without a global splitting and the intrinsic scheme-theoretic Fitting/Picard identity. ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence, its reduced constant-h⁰ projective-bundle model, and the scheme-theoretic ordered/unordered comparison on Conf₆. SRC-0004 fixes the essential convention W_f=(O(2)⊗γ*O(-f))|_C. FND-0105 is retained as the explicit normalization hypothesis. FND-0125 supplies the normalization-free exclusion of hyperelliptic-composed covers from the balanced splitting, and FND-0130 supplies the plane-quintic CE exclusion used below.

## Proved steps

1. Write O_C(D)=γ*O(1). Hypothesis (N) gives O(1)|_C≅ω_{C/S}⊗γ*O(2); therefore W_5≅ω_{C/S}^{⊗2}(-D) and L≅ω_{C/S}(-D). On a geometric fibre, O(D) has degree four and at least two sections. Clifford gives h⁰(O(D))≤3. Equality would be Clifford equality, so C would be hyperelliptic and every pencil in |D| would factor as γ=q∘h. FND-0125 then gives relations splitting O(2)⊕O(7), contradicting O(4)⊕O(5). Thus h⁰(O(D))=2. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality now give h¹(L)=2 and h⁰(L)=1+h¹(L)=3. In particular the h⁰=4 branch is empty.

2. Since S is reduced and both fibre dimensions are constant, Grauert gives π_*L locally free of rank three, R¹π_*L locally free of rank two, and base change. ATT-0066 identifies the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence canonically with I≅P_S((π_*L)^∨). Hence I→S is a Zariski-locally trivial P²-bundle, smooth and proper of pure relative dimension two.

3. The bundle L is base-point-free. Indeed, a base point p would make L(-p) a g²_5. The genus-six classification used in FND-0130 forces the smooth plane-quintic case; because L=ω(-D), the given tetragonal pencil is projection from p. The CE restriction calculation in FND-0130 makes that projection splitting unbalanced, contradicting (BAL). Thus |L_s| is base-point-free on every geometric fibre. In characteristic zero its associated morphism to P² is separable, so Bertini gives a reduced general hyperplane pullback. Consequently V_s is a nonempty dense open of |L_s|≅P² for every s. This uses base-point-freeness and Bertini, not χ(L)=1.

4. ATT-0066 identifies the pullback of I to Conf₆ with Z_ev as an equality of ideals, not merely of geometric points. Because Conf₆ already imposes distinct support, this pullback is the ordered incidence over V. Ordering six distinct points gives a finite étale S₆-torsor Z_ev→V. The deck action is free: a permutation fixing an ordered tuple of six pairwise-distinct points is the identity. This statement concerns the deck group only and says nothing about automorphisms of the marked curve.

5. The open V is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two, and finite étale pullback shows that Z_ev is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two. Conf₆(C/S) is S-smooth of relative dimension six. Since the Abel–Jacobi/Fitting identity makes Z_ev closed in Conf₆, a closed immersion between S-smooth schemes is regular. The relative dimension difference is four, so the conormal is locally free of rank four; the conormal sequence splits locally because Ω_{Z_ev/S} is locally free. This lci conclusion comes from relative smoothness, not from determinantal expected codimension.

6. For each irreducible component S_α, the projective bundle I_α is irreducible, and V_α=V∩I_α is nonempty open and hence irreducible and dense. Thus components of I and V correspond to those of S and have dimension dim(S_α)+2 when finite-dimensional. For a component T of Z_ev, flatness of the finite étale map makes the contraction of its generic point a generic point of V; finiteness then makes T→V_α surjective. Hence dim(T)=dim(V_α)=dim(S_α)+2. The number of such T over V_α is not determined without additional normality and monodromy input.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment is used to establish a universal claim.

## Remaining scope

The proof is relative over a reduced scheme base. It does not descend the projective-bundle argument to a stack base, determine moduli inertia, or establish any closed embedding, absolute codimension, Gysin morphism, or Tate statement in M_{6,6}.

claims.justification: Normalization gives L=ω(-D). Clifford leaves h⁰(O(D))∈{2,3}; the equality case is hyperelliptic-composed, which FND-0125 proves has relations splitting O(2)⊕O(7), contradicting balance. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality give the remaining dimensions.
claims.statement: Under (BAL)+(N), every geometric fibre has L≅ω(-D), h⁰(O(D))=2, h⁰(L)=3, and h¹(L)=2; hence the h⁰=4 stratum is empty.

claims.justification: CLM-0094-1 gives constant h⁰=3 and h¹=2. Grauert gives local freeness and base change, and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4,5 gives the canonical incidence/projective-bundle identification. A projective bundle with irreducible fibre has exactly the inverse images of the base components as its irreducible components.
claims.statement: Over reduced S, the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence is a P²-bundle I≅P_S((π_*L)^∨), and its irreducible components correspond to those of S.

claims.justification: A base point would produce a g²_5 and hence the plane-quintic projection case, excluded from the balanced CE locus by FND-0130. Characteristic-zero Bertini applied to the resulting base-point-free system produces reduced general members.
claims.statement: L is fibrewise base-point-free, and the distinct-support open V is nonempty and dense in every P² fibre.

claims.justification: ATT-0065 gives the Fitting/Picard ideal identity and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6 gives the ordered distinct-support comparison and stack-level torsor. Pairwise distinctness makes the permutation action free.
claims.statement: On Conf₆, Z_ev is scheme-theoretically the ordered incidence over V, and Z_ev→V is a finite étale S₆-torsor with free deck action.

claims.justification: V is an open of a P²-bundle and Z_ev→V is finite étale, while Conf₆→S is smooth of relative dimension six. The closed immersion between S-smooth schemes is regular, with codimension equal to the relative-dimension difference.
claims.statement: Z_ev→S is smooth of pure relative dimension two, and Z_ev↪Conf₆(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four with locally free rank-four conormal.

claims.justification: For a finite flat map, a minimal prime contracts to a minimal prime; the finite image containing the generic point is the entire target component. Finite morphisms preserve dimension, and V_α is dense open in the P²-bundle over S_α.
claims.statement: Every irreducible component of Z_ev maps finitely and surjectively onto an irreducible component V_α and has dimension dim(S_α)+2 whenever S_α is finite-dimensional.

gap_markers: Irreducibility of the balanced base S and the number of irreducible components of Z_ev are not determined.
Full S₆ monodromy, including a transposition and the required occurrence loci, remains unproved.
The projective-bundle and regular-immersion theorem is not extended here to nonreduced or stack bases.
Stabilizers Aut(C,Γ) and Aut(C,γ,Γ), and the faithfulness, quasi-finiteness, closedness, and codimension of the forgetful map to M_{6,6}, remain undetermined.
No absolute dimension, closed pure-codimension-four embedding, lci/Gysin statement, or closure analysis is proved inside M_{6,6}; unbalanced CE strata remain outside the theorem.
The weak relative-canonical normalization (N), residual hypothesis (R), and ambient equation-bundle freeness remain external where applicable.
Positive characteristic and all Hodge, weight, purity, and Tate consequences for RED-0001 remain untreated.
novelty_claims: A single scope-consistent composition determines the relative component dimensions, finite-cover structure, smoothness, and regular codimension-four embedding of the balanced ordered failure locus without promoting it to a global locus in M_{6,6}.

summary: The balanced normalized relative failure locus is a smooth relative twofold and regular codimension-four closed subscheme of the ordered configuration space. Its unordered model is a fibrewise-dense open in a P²-bundle, and ordering is a finite étale S₆-torsor. Relative component dimensions are determined, but component counts, moduli stabilizers, and the map to M_{6,6} remain unresolved.

theorem_scope.base: Reduced locally Noetherian scheme over a characteristic-zero field.
theorem_scope.configuration_scope: The Fitting/Abel–Jacobi equality is asserted only on Conf₆, where the six sections are ordered and pairwise disjoint.
theorem_scope.exclusions: Nonreduced or stack bases; irreducibility of the balanced Hurwitz base; full S₆ monodromy; the number of components of Z_ev; stabilizers Aut(C,Γ) or Aut(C,γ,Γ); the forgetful morphism to M_{6,6}; absolute dimension, closure, codimension, lci, or Gysin properties in M_{6,6}; unbalanced strata; ambient equation-bundle freeness; and all Hodge/Tate conclusions.
theorem_scope.finite_cover_scope: The S₆ assertion is a torsor assertion for ordered distinct divisors, hence also at stack level; it is not a coarse-moduli quotient assertion.
theorem_scope.generality: Relative balanced degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl families with the canonical nonsplit filtration and explicit weak normalization (N).

theorem_statement: Let k be a characteristic-zero field and S a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme. Let π:C→S be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-six curves equipped with a finite flat degree-four map γ:C→P¹_S, the standard degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl resolution, fibrewise balanced relations bundle F_s≅O(4)⊕O(5), its canonical filtration with quotient W_5 of degree 16, and the weak relative-canonical normalization (N). Put L=W_5⊗ω_{C/S}^{-1}, let I=Hilb⁶(C/S)×_{Pic⁶(C/S)}S be the Abel–Jacobi incidence over [L], let V=I^{dist} be its distinct-support open, and let Z_ev⊂Conf₆(C/S) be the intrinsic evaluation-failure scheme. Then every geometric fibre has h⁰(L_s)=3 and h¹(L_s)=2; I≅P_S((π_*L)^∨) is a P²-bundle; V is nonempty and dense in every fibre; and Z_ev is scheme-theoretically the ordered incidence over V. The morphism Z_ev→V is a finite étale S₆-torsor with free deck action, Z_ev→S is smooth of pure relative dimension two, and Z_ev↪Conf₆(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four with locally free conormal of rank four. Irreducible components of I and V correspond to irreducible components of S; every irreducible component of Z_ev maps finitely and surjectively onto one component of V and, over a finite-dimensional component S_α, has dimension dim(S_α)+2. No count of the components of Z_ev is asserted.
